chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
As you approach or during retirement, your property often becomes your main asset - and a lever for quality of life. Reduce size (downsizing), free up cash or generate income: several options are available to you.

This guide explores real estate strategies for retirement, with their advantages and points to watch out for.

Informative content, not financial advice: consult your advisors. Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

As you approach or during retirement, your property often becomes your main asset - and a lever for quality of life. This guide explores downsizing, ways to generate income, the transfer and adaptation of housing for aging in place.

Informative content, not financial advice: consult the professionals concerned.

chapters.title: Downsizing: reducing to live better
chapters.objective: Weigh the benefit of reducing the size.
chapters.html:
Weigh the benefit of reducing the size.

Selling a large house for a smaller property (condo, smaller house) can transform your daily life.

  • Less maintenance, taxes and energy costs.
  • Potential liquidity released by the price difference.
  • A simplified life, often better adapted.

It is often a choice of quality of life as much as financial. To evaluate all the same: transaction and moving costs, and attachment to the house.

Selling a large house for a smaller one (condo, reduced house) reduces maintenance, taxes and energy, frees up cash flow and simplifies life. It is often a quality of life choice as much as a financial one; weigh transaction costs and attachment to home.

Emilie's advice

Downsizing is not just about money. Many retirees tell me above all that they have saved time and peace of mind. Weigh the comfort of life as much as the financial calculation.

chapters.title: Generate income or free up cash
chapters.objective: Put your real estate assets to work.
chapters.html:
Put your real estate assets to work.

Your property can become a lever of income in retirement:

  • Downsizing + placement : invest the difference for income.
  • Income property : generate rents (with the management that this implies).
  • Enhancement of equity of the residence (certain loans adapted to seniors): to be examined with caution.

Each option has tax and risk implications: the objective is income sustainable, not a bet.

Your property can become a lever of income: downsizing + investment of the difference, income property (with the management that this implies), or solutions for enhancing equity (to be examined with caution). Each option has tax and risk implications: aim for sustainable income, not a gamble.

Emilie's advice

Be wary of “miracle” solutions to turn your house into cash. Some are expensive in long-term interest. Always have it validated by an independent advisor.

chapters.title: Think about transmission and the long term
chapters.objective: Integrate real estate into your estate planning.
chapters.html:
Integrate real estate into your estate planning.

Your property is part of the heritage that you will transmit. Thinking about it early avoids many complications for your loved ones:

  • Will up to date.
  • Taxation of the estate.
  • Equity between heirs.

Coordinate your real estate decisions with your overall financial and estate planning, ideally with a notary and a planner.

Your property is part of the heritage to be transmitted: thinking early about the transmission (will, inheritance taxation, equity between heirs) avoids complications for your loved ones. Talk about it during your lifetime: a house to be shared between several children is a classic source of conflict.

Emilie's advice

Talk about your intentions to your loved ones during your lifetime. A house that must be shared between several children is a classic source of conflict - which clarity easily prevents.

chapters.title: Staying at home: adapting the property
chapters.html:
Aging at home safely.

Not everyone wants to move. Staying in your own property can be a great choice, provided youadapt :

  • Reduce obstacles (steps, thresholds, bathtub).
  • Improve lighting and security (grab bars, non-slip).
  • Provide forinterview entrusted to services if necessary.

Anticipating these arrangements means peacefully prolonging the pleasure of living at home.

Staying at home can be an excellent choice, provided you adapt the property: reduce obstacles (steps, thresholds, bathtub), improve lighting and security, provide delegated maintenance. These arrangements cost little and change everything for aging at home in safety.

Emilie's advice

Small safety features cost little and change everything for aging at home. Think about it before you need it: a suitable bathroom is better than an avoidable fall.

chapters.title: Building your real estate retirement strategy
chapters.objective: Decide based on your quality of life and safety.
chapters.html:
Decide according to your quality of life and your safety.

There is no single solution: the right strategy is the one that corresponds to YOUR situation. A simple process:

  1. Clarify your needs (space, costs, income, autonomy).
  2. Estimate the equity in your property.
  3. Compare options (downsizing, income, staying at home).
  4. Coordinate with your financial and estate plan.

Decide with professional lighting, but always according to your life priorities.

There is no single solution: the right strategy corresponds to YOUR situation. Start with “how do I want to live my retirement?” ”, then follow up with real estate. Estimate your net worth, compare options and coordinate with your financial and estate plan.

Emilie's advice

Start with the question “how do I want to live my retirement?” ”, then follow up with real estate. The house is a means of serving your life project, not the other way around.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Clarify my retirement needs (space, costs, income).
  2. Estimate the equity in my property.

Within 30 days

  1. Explore downsizing and income options with an advisor.
  2. Review my estate planning with a notary.

Then

  1. Decide on a strategy aligned with my quality of life and my safety.

For my strategy

  1. Clarify my retirement needs and estimate my home equity.
  2. Compare downsizing, income and staying at home with an advisor.
